Subject: Re: [ALERT] p95 latency spike - mux-concurrency pool (us-west)

Team —
We have an active customer-visible p95 jump for BrightCart (their checkout gen calls). Monitoring attached the p95 report. No increase in 5xx which suggests queuing/backpressure or KV cache behavior rather than a downstream failure.

Immediate asks:
1) Ben / SRE: can you confirm cache hit rates, queue lengths, and autoscaler behavior for the last 30m? Is this correlated with a concurrency burst from BrightCart (they were doing a marketing flash)?
2) Karthik / Eng: if a routing or model-variant downgrade gives us a quick latency win, what is the safe rollback/revert window and risk to quality?
3) Marissa / Product: we need a 1-2 paragraph customer-facing status for Michael at BrightCart; advise tone and whether to quantify minutes to mitigation.

I'm proposing a quick technical huddle (15 min) at 08:25 UTC to align on an active mitigation and the customer readout. If we need to enable a temporary model variant or throttling, call it out — we'll need exec visibility.

Attachments: p95_report_20270420.csv

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability (acting)
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T08:22:10Z
Subject: Re: Concurrency surge: triage matrix, mitigation plan, and customer readout

Quick triage notes (observed):
- KV cache hit-rate for mux-concurrency shard us-west dropped from 86% to ~51% starting 07:36 — aligns with the p95 jump.
- Autoscaler scaled new workers but they entered steady-state warmup; cold KV warmup + large fanout from one customer caused queueing at the routing layer.
- No 5xx spike; inference runtime CPU/GPU healthy.

Short-term mitigations I'm recommending now (low-risk):
A) Enable KV warmstart for the affected shard to pre-populate prefixes (takes ~7-10m to warm).
B) Raise soft concurrency limit for BrightCart routing key from 100 -> 140 for 30 minutes to absorb backlog while warmstart completes.
C) If A+B insufficient within 15m, route 25% of BrightCart traffic to a lower-memory model variant (gpt-base-quant) to reduce token latency; requires product sign-off.

I'll run A immediately and open the routing change as RFC INF-4721 (linked). Will monitor and post updated p95 in 5/10/15 minute marks.

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, michael.lee@brightcart.com
Date: 2027-04-20T09:15:01Z
Subject: Re: Concurrency surge: triage matrix, mitigation plan, and customer readout

Thanks Ben — good signal. A couple of product-context notes:
- BrightCart is highly sensitive to latency during checkout; they prioritize p95 under 250ms and are on our reserved capacity plan. Any model fallback must preserve semantic fidelity for short prompts (checkout summarization).
- On the roadmap side, the long-term fix is a combination of prefix caching improvements + a smaller quantized model family for bursty traffic. We don't have bandwidth to ship the quantized fallback this week without extra SRE support.

My asks:
1) If Ben's A+B returns p95 < 300ms, let's hold on fallback and send a conservative customer readout.
2) If we need fallback (C), product approves a phased 25% route to gpt-base-quant but asks for automated quality checks against a small prompt set before routing. Who can own that check?

Draft customer message (short, non-technical):
"Michael — we observed an atypical spike in request concurrency which temporarily increased response times for some checkout requests. We have applied mitigations and are monitoring. We expect response times to normalize within 20 minutes and will follow up with a short post-incident summary and prevention plan."

I'll prepare the post-incident summary template once we stabilize.

-Marissa Cole
Product Manager, Serving Experience
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-20T11:50:12Z
Subject: Re: Concurrency surge: triage matrix, mitigation plan, and customer readout

Status update and mitigation plan (ETA):
- Ben's warmstart (A) completed at 08:32 and improved cache hit-rate to ~74% by 08:42. Raising concurrency (B) applied at 08:10 and held steady; together these reduced p95 from ~600ms to ~280ms by 09:05.
- Observed a second small re-burst at 10:12 localized to a BrightCart shard; warmstart + routing adjustments again dropped p95 to ~240ms.

Planned technical action (we can do within 30-45m):
1) Deploy model-variant routing rule: send 25% of BrightCart traffic to gpt-base-quant in us-west only. This requires toggling an existing routing flag, automatic A/B quality checks (we'll run 50 prompt checks/minute comparing latency + a small NLU-quality score), and a rollback guard if quality degrades >3% on the checks.
2) SRE to monitor p95 and the A/B quality checks for 20 minutes; if no regression, escalate to 50% for up to 1 hour.

Risks: small potential quality delta for edge cases (e.g., unusual prompts). Rollback can be instantaneous via routing flag. I will own the change and the JIRA INF-4721 will capture the roll forward/rollback.

Planned customer readout (Grace): see attached customer_readout_draft.txt — I've annotated the tech bits that are safe to surface.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
